partitions.reason: At identical u and h, the dev rows with constant positive versus negative histories have markedly different responses. This tests whether separating current state from the full prior record can explain that contrast.

At the same u and h, distinct histories produce substantially different response levels. Grouping current drive with history tests a partition not captured by the failed additive forms' separate current-drive and history contributions.

These fresh observations vary history at matched u and h, while other fresh rows vary h at matched u and history. Grouping lag and history together tests whether their combined contribution is incompatible with additive separation from current drive.

remaining_uncertainties: The reported C5 and C6 dev RMSE values alone do not establish failure of any broader additive-separation class; exact partition RMSEs remain to be computed.
Partition tests can establish empirical adequacy on supplied rows, not a unique mechanism or generalization beyond them.

verified.proof: Allow unrestricted values for A and B at every unique group input. Their prediction vectors span the incidence matrix columns. The exact rational projection residual is orthogonal to all columns. Pythagoras proves its SSE is the global minimum for every shared deterministic additive function on these records.
verified.scope: Empirical RMSE on these exact rows, not a universal physical theorem or a noise-only bound
